title: Python snapshots the previous request's root before applying this request's environment
trigger: The context variable is set from `os.environ` **before** `_apply_request_runtime(req)`. It is not populated from this request's environment. A warm A cell makes the original suspended-cell regression pass, but the next request still snapshots A before installing B. Executed with real manager adoptions and real Python backend calls. The concurrent control suspends A, adopts B, reads from B, then resumes A.
measured:
warm A
adopt B; read artifact://8 -> ROOT A, exit 0
adopt C; read artifact://8 -> ROOT B, exit 0
how_found_quote: Executed with real manager adoptions and real Python backend calls

title: a root-specific miss still delegates to the session's newer root after the final listing
trigger: 1. Start and suspend a real A cell asking for `artifact://1`; adopt C and execute another cell. 2. Let the host finish its stable A listing, which correctly misses id 1. 3. Hold the real tool reply at the worker transport. Run and finish a real copy adding A's `1.read.log`. 4. Deliver the already-produced empty reply. 5. The helper delegates the URI to the current `ReadTool`, which resolves C, not the root A that the request carried.
how_found_quote: Hold the real tool reply at the worker transport. Run and finish a real copy adding A's `1.read.log`. ... Deliver the already-produced empty reply.

title: a background Python read inherits the newest cell's cancellation and status ownership
trigger: An A cell completes after starting a background reader. B completes with its own signal. Aborting **B's** signal after completion makes A's subsequent no-copy read fail. With B still active, A's reader waits through a real pending copy. The probe waits for the actual abort-listener attachment, then aborts B.
how_found_quote: The probe waits for the actual abort-listener attachment, then aborts B.

title: any nonempty unknown Python run can use the session fallback for ordinary tools
trigger: The actual loopback server was registered for one run, that run was removed, and an ordinary `read` request was sent with `run:"never-registered"`. The real `ReadTool` executed and returned a result. An empty-run ordinary request is still rejected with HTTP 400, so checking only that case misses the bypass.
how_found_quote: The actual loopback server was registered for one run, that run was removed, and an ordinary `read` request was sent with `run:"never-registered"`.

title: standing Python registrations are not scoped or retired with the kernel that owns them
trigger: Two retained kernels use the same eval session identity but different cwd keys and logical owners. B registers last and leaves a real background thread. Disposing **A's owner** removes B's standing entry; B remains alive but its thread receives `No active Python tool bridge session`. A real `python.kernelMode: per-call` cell prints its actual `py-bridge:<uuid>` identity; after the cell and its kernel have ended, the server still answers readiness for that exact identity. `disposePyToolBridge()` clears the old run map, but not the new session map.
measured: OTHER_KERNEL_ALIVE {"answer":{"error":"No active Python tool bridge session: python:c8abf527-e281-4a60-a01f-4c04adc139d0:"}}
how_found_quote: Two retained kernels use the same eval session identity but different cwd keys and logical owners. B registers last and leaves a real background thread. Disposing **A's owner** removes B's standing entry; B remains alive

title: JavaScript treats an error containing the run-gone phrase as proof that the run ended
trigger: `message.includes("Run no longer active")` is not a check for the host's specific run-gone response. The new bound error includes the directory, so a directory with that phrase produces a matching error without the run having ended. A public EvalTool using a real directory named `Run no longer active` performs sixteen overlapping real copies. Its genuine bound error switches it into run-less resolution. The probe aborts at listing 17.
how_found_quote: performs sixteen overlapping real copies. Its genuine bound error switches it into run-less resolution. The probe aborts at listing **17**.

title: the new completed-overlap repository test does not reject the old pending-only algorithm
trigger: The hook finishes the copy **before** obtaining the actual directory names. Its returned listing is fresh, not the stale snapshot in the incident. A discrimination control ran the pending-only algorithm against that hook and it returned `1.read.log` successfully with **one** listing. Changing the hook to capture names first, then copy, then return the captured names made the same algorithm return a miss.
how_found_quote: A discrimination control ran the pending-only algorithm against that hook and it returned `1.read.log` successfully with **one** listing.
